To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the organic anion transporter OAT1/3 mediates renal excretion of the ginkgo constituents ginkgolide A, B, and C and bilobalides.

(i) ginkgolide B, ginkgolde M and bilobalid are substrates of the organic anion transporter-1 (OAT1) and OAT3, (ii) the renal clearance of ginkgoides and bilobalides are increased by OAT1/3 inhibitors, (iii) OAT1/ OAT3 inhibition does not influence the pharmacokinetics of ginkgoids and bilobalids, and
the organic anion transporter (OAT) 1 and OAT3 are involved in the renal excretion of the main constituents of the Ginkgo biloba extract.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pharmacokinetics, metabolism and excretion of the ginkgolide constituents of Ginkgo biloba L. in rats and mice.
the pharmacological effects of Ginkgo biloba extract on the cardiovascular system and its mechanisms, and with the clinical application of Ginkgo in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases.
the effects of Ginkgo biloba on the human brain, and with the possible use of Ginkgo as an aid for the treatment of dementia, especially Alzheimer's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ginkgo biloba leaf extract is a safe and effective treatment for dementia.
the pharmacological effects of the ginkgo biloba extract EGb 761 are due to the ginkgolide and bilobalane content of the extract, and not to the flavonoid and terpene content.
the pharmacological effects of Ginkgo biloba are due to the presence of flavonoids and terpene lactones in the extract.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the influence of OAT1/3 on pharmacokinetics of ginkgolic acids is not as important as the influence of Oatp1a/1c on pharmacokinetics, but the influence of Oats on the renal excretion of bilobalide is very strong.
the pharmacokinetics of ginkgoides in humans is not influenced by OATP1/3.
the use of a standardized extract of G. biloba (EGb 761®) is not associated with any significant adverse effects.
